source.reason: Overall microstructure of the pre-strained + heat-treated SPCC specimen derived from the discussion of the Cottrell effect, dislocation release and recovery.

overall_structure.value: Mild steel SPCC (Fe matrix). Before deformation, dislocations are locked by carbon and other solutes due to the Cottrell effect. During 15% plastic deformation the dislocations are released from the Cottrell effect and move with lower internal stress, changing the dislocation structure; because the diffusion rate of C in an Fe matrix is very low at room temperature the Cottrell atmosphere is not recovered by plastic deformation alone. The subsequent heat treatment (373 K, 90 h) recovers only the Cottrell atmosphere by C diffusion while keeping dislocations stationary, restraining the movable dislocations.

source.reason: Grain-boundary dislocation pile-up behaviour relevant to the pre-strained + heat-treated sample.
The paper describes dislocation pile-up against grain boundaries and the associated modulus decrease near the boundary, which is the key defect interaction.

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Dislocations released from a common source move along the same slip surface and easily pile up, the front of the dislocations being stopped by obstacles such as grain boundaries and solutes. The pile-up dislocations can move backwards when the shearing stress is released during unloading, causing the apparent elastic modulus to decrease. The nano-indentation results show the elastic modulus near the boundary has a smaller value than in other regions, i.e. a decrease near the boundary area (X ≈ 5–10 μm of the scanning line).

slip_behavior.value: Dislocations released from a common source move along the same slip surface and pile up; pile-up dislocations can move backwards when the shearing stress is released during unloading.

interface_notes.value: Pile-up of dislocations is considered to occur near the boundary of grains, so movable dislocations have a greater possibility of existence there than in other partitions; the apparent elastic modulus can differ from the boundary to the centre of a grain.

unmapped_findings: Specimen C shows the largest discrepancy between the two modulus ranges (along with B): 186 (0–0.05% strain) vs 162 (whole elastic range), which the paper attributes to the recovery of the Cottrell effect restraining the movable dislocations.

The gradient of the stress–strain curve for the pre-strained + heat-treated workpiece (C) shows a unique manner: it decreases from the beginning (like the pre-strained workpiece), then increases to almost the same level as the annealed workpiece, giving a larger average elastic modulus than the other pre-strained workpiece.

The heat treatment (373 K for 90 h) was designed so that only the Cottrell atmosphere is recovered by C diffusion while dislocations remain stationary, allowing confirmation of the effect of movable dislocations on the apparent elastic modulus.
